How much does car battery replacement cost?

A new 12-volt battery, installed — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$456–$493

Labor $61–$90 · parts $394–$403

Bay Area: no published metro-specific figure found — the national range is the honest reference.

Why quotes run $150 to $500

Battery type
Standard lead-acid $75–$175; AGM $150–$300. Start-stop cars need AGM — downgrading causes real problems.
Installation
DIY: $0. Parts stores: usually free with purchase. A shop charges $30–$75; dealers more.
Size & power
Bigger group sizes and higher cold-cranking amps add $20–$100. Buy the group size in the manual — close enough isn't.
Warranty
Each extra year of warranty adds roughly $15–$30. A longer warranty usually means a better-built battery, not just marketing.

Same battery, different bill

Parts store / DIY
$75–$250

Warehouse clubs have the lowest prices; most parts stores install free with purchase. You handle the core return.

Shop / dealer
$150–$300+

You pay for labor ($30–$75+) and their markup. Worth it for buried batteries or cars that need registration after install.

Bottom line: if the battery is under the hood and held by one bracket, buy it at a parts store and let them install it free. Pay a shop only when access is miserable.

Common questions

How long do car batteries last?

Three to five years. Heat kills them faster than cold — in hot climates, test annually after year three.

How do I know it's the battery and not the alternator?

Get both tested — most parts stores do it free. A battery that won't hold a charge after a full charge is done; one that keeps dying may be a victim, not the culprit.

What does AGM mean and do I need it?

Absorbed glass mat — tougher, longer-lived, required by start-stop systems. If the manual or the old battery says AGM, match it.

Can I install it myself?

Usually yes: two terminals, one hold-down, ten minutes. Some European cars need the new battery registered to the car — that's a shop job.

Every car prices differently.
